investigators: Gawlikowski, Juchniewicz, al-Zahrani (Polish Centre of Mediterranean Archaeology / Saudi Commission)
depth_note: Harbour installations, a large storehouse (khans), two necropoleis
key_finds: 25 excavated coins (24 bronze, 1 silver), Obodas III to Tiberius, 2nd c. BC - AD 40; Nabataean pottery; inscriptions
NO Nabataean or Roman remains found. Burton reported ruins in 1879; the 1981 survey did not confirm them.
source: Ingraham et al. 1981: 78, cited in Juchniewicz PAM 26/2 2018: 32

investigators: F. A. Khan (Pakistan Dept of Archaeology); later Pakistani-Italian-French mission
depth_note: Virgin soil never reached: heavy water infiltration stopped the trenches
key_finds: Scytho-Parthian levels below the Sasanian and Islamic town; Red Polished Ware of the 1st c. BC - 2nd c. AD from the earliest levels; Scytho-Parthian coins reported but not catalogued
source: Felici et al.; Mughal 2018, Pakistan Archaeology 33

depth_note: Bedrock has not been located under the whole city; deep soundings only. Accumulated deposits have long prevented excavation reaching the earliest levels.
key_finds: c. 600 coins from IMTO excavations plus c. 1,300 coin blanks from the first campaigns, supporting a mint on site; the blanks have never been analysed

depth_note: Ptolemaic occupation suspected 'well below the current water table'
key_finds: 153 coins and one lead token from the Chicago seasons; only 14 coins from 1999-2003 deemed identifiable enough to publish; Roman waterfront of late 1st c. BC - early 3rd c. AD built by reclaiming mangrove swamp

depth_note: Bedrock reached in places; Ptolemaic water channels cut into bedrock recorded
key_finds: 115 coins published to date, of which only 16 Ptolemaic; coins from the Ptolemaic fort still unpublished; c. 650 beads and pendants from the 2014-15 seasons

depth_note: Surveys and excavations at necropoleis; no systematic research before 2017
key_finds: Imported material is 99% of all artefacts documented; Roman, Parthian and South Arabian imports of the 1st-3rd c. AD

depth_note: 61 trenches, about 1% of the mound; core area 45 ha
key_finds: 6,029 Roman amphora sherds, 122 terra sigillata, 3,098 torpedo jar, 1,527 TGP, 8,534 Rouletted Ware against 3,537,464 local sherds; 98 coins; 38,718 glass beads

investigators: K. V. Soundara Rajan, K. V. Raman, N. G. Unnithan (ASI Southern Circle with Kerala Dept)
depth_note: Trial digs at five localities: Karuppadana, Kilattali, Mathilakam, Tirukkulasekharapuram, Tiruvanjikulam
key_finds: All material 9th-11th c. Chera. The following volume records the digs 'had not yielded any tangible evidence'.

investigators: P. Narayana Babu, M. Raman Namboodiri (ASI Southern Circle)
depth_note: Survey of Malappuram and Palghat districts explicitly 'investigating for the sites showing Roman contact in the Ponnani valley'
key_finds: Megalithic topikal burials at Alancode, Ongallur, Ponumundum, Tennala, Thannairkod, Thavanur; menhirs near Thirunavaya. NO Roman material.
Russet-coated ware on a red-slipped bowl from a laterite rock-cut cave at Kuttippala; umbrella stones, menhirs, urn burials

depth_note: Reported alongside the Cranganore negative result
key_finds: Russet-coated (wavy line) Painted Ware, which 'overlaps with the megalithic Black-and-red Ware in the early centuries of the Christian era'; the compiler calls it 'of great significance'

depth_note: Survey; structures of cut ashlar and coral recorded, cisterns cut into limestone bedrock
key_finds: Sherds and glass bangles from cemeteries
